title: Understanding AOP
context: What is AOP, and how does Spring apply it?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Aspect-oriented programming moves cross-cutting concerns, such as logging, transactions, security and metrics, out of business code into aspects. Spring applies aspects at run time with proxies. A bean is wrapped in a proxy, and calls to its public methods run advice before, after or around the real method. Spring AOP only intercepts calls that go through the proxy, so self-calls inside a class are not advised.

points.title: Cross-cutting concerns
points.why: Logging, transactions and security are kept out of the business methods.

points.title: Proxy limits
points.why: Calls that bypass the proxy, such as this.method(), don't get advice.
